solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Promiscuous relationships producing victims

parts.note: promiscuous liaisons are casual, with no commitment
ties are bonds or relationships between people

explanation.surface: A warning that sleeping around leaves people hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Casualties are the people killed or injured in an accident or war, its victims.

clue.text: Blinking thing perhaps gets one effing and blinding loudly

indicators.note: something said loudly is heard, so we want the sound of the word

parts.note: effing and blinding is British slang for swearing, so the swearer is a curser

explanation.surface: A sweary person blinking in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blinking' is a mild British swear-word in the surface but describes the flashing marker on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursor is the flashing marker on a computer screen showing where typing will go.

clue.text: Windows operating system may include these five tests following launch of server

definitions.text: Windows operating system may include these

indicators.note: the cricket series follows the opening letter
the launch of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Ashes is the England v Australia cricket series, traditionally five Test matches

explanation.surface: Computer jargon: Windows software tested five times after its server goes live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows operating system' suggests Microsoft but means how real windows open: sash windows slide up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashes are the sliding frames of a sash window, the mechanism by which it opens.

clue.text: Direct rocket's nose to separate over the moon, according to rhyme?

indicators.note: the single letter is put in to separate two letters of the rhyme phrase

parts.words: over the moon, according to rhyme?
parts.note: in Hey Diddle Diddle the cow jumped over the moon, so going over it is how the cow flies

indicators.note: a rocket's nose is its front, so its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to aim a spacecraft so it parts from its launcher and passes the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes between C and OW of AS THE COW FLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: As the crow flies means in a straight line, by the most direct route.

clue.text: Stationer's bizarre wigs

indicators.note: bizarre suggests the letters are made strange, jumbled

parts.note: the shop owner's title, with the 's read as is, a link

explanation.surface: A stationery shop selling strange hairpieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wigs' is the British verb to wig, scold, not hairpieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To wig someone is to scold them severely, the same as tearing into them.

clue.text: More than one way to leave lover, once getting possessive

definitions.text: More than one way to leave

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
its is the possessive form of it

explanation.surface: Ways to walk out on a partner who has grown possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are doorways or routes out, plural for more than one.

clue.text: Sent away from edges of promenade for hairstyle

indicators.note: the word is sent away from both edges of the promenade word, its first two letters off the front and last two off the back

parts.note: a seafront is a seaside promenade
the four letters of the clue word itself are the ones removed, split across the two ends

explanation.surface: Someone banished from the seaside walkway because of their haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAFRONT loses SE from the front and NT from the back, the two halves of SENT, leaving the middle four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Escape trial with extreme dispatch

parts.note: to flee is to escape
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A defendant running off from court in a great hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetest is the superlative of fleet, swift, so moving with the greatest speed.

clue.text: Sons use drug company rearing spiders?

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing means rising up, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to do a drug is to use it
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: Sons using drugs while a firm raises arachnids.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits spiders are not octopods, only that they too have eight legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopods are creatures with eight limbs, as spiders also are, by a playful stretch.

clue.text: Sign that wedding's to be battle arena

parts.note: an engagement is a military battle
a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A gloomy joke that marriage will be a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement ring is worn to show that a couple are betrothed and plan to marry.

clue.text: Shock reversal — tried again

indicators.note: reversal tells us to read the stun-gun word from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: a Taser delivers an electric shock

explanation.surface: A surprising turnaround in a court case that went to retrial.
explanation.definitionFit: Resat is the past tense of resit, to take an exam again, so tried again.

clue.text: Order a side of nachos in melting fondue

indicators.note: fondue is French for melted, so the letters are melted down and recast
a side of the snack word here is its first letter, its front edge

parts.note: taken as written as part of the pool

explanation.surface: A diner orders a side of nachos dunked in a pot of melted cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the diner placing an order, but it is the definition; 'fondue' is the anagram signal for A, N and MELTING together.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is the arrangement of things in a line or proper order.

clue.text: Unity ahead after division?

definitions.meaning: unity is the state of being one whole
split the word ahead into a head: a is one, and a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A rallying cry that togetherness lies in the future, once a split is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Divide 'ahead' into A HEAD: A = ONE and a headland = NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is the quality of being single and undivided, the same idea as unity.

clue.text: Found drink to be laced with acid

indicators.note: a drink laced with something has it mixed in, so the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: to sup is to drink
tart means sharp or acid in taste

explanation.surface: Discovering that someone's drink has been spiked with LSD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as discovered, but it is the verb to found, establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up a business is to found or establish it.

clue.text: Violent grans, locked outside, broke the law

indicators.note: the locked word sits outside, wrapping the rearranged grannies

parts.note: tressed means having locks or tresses of hair

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Aggressive grannies shut out of the house turned to crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locked' looks like shut in, but here it means having locks of hair; 'Violent' turns the grannies into ANSGR, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to break a law or rule, so the past tense matches broke the law.

clue.text: Playing, gets into a baby carriage

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A child at play climbs into a pram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby carriage' looks like a pram but means the carrying of a baby in the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the period of carrying a developing baby in the womb, a pregnancy.

clue.text: Ace paragraph about cattle's cut in — quite good

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: the cattle word has the two letters spelling in cut out

parts.note: bovine means about or relating to cattle

explanation.surface: A clumsy note on a paragraph about cattle that was inserted into a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in' tells us to remove IN from BOVINE, leaving BOVE; the blog reads PAR as wrapping it, but the letters run in plain order.
explanation.definitionFit: Above par, from golf and finance, means better than average, so fairly good.

clue.text: Dozes after school, comprehending power in alcohol

indicators.note: the dozes come after the school abbreviation
comprehending means including, so the power letter goes inside

parts.note: naps are short dozes
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Pupils nodding off after lessons, the energy of drink inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a kind of alcohol often flavoured with fruit.

clue.text: Lords not turning out to support ladies admitting excesses

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: the ladies admit the excesses, taking them inside

parts.note: ladies are women
ODs are overdoses, excesses of a drug

explanation.surface: Peers who stay home, propped up by their wives through their indulgences.
explanation.walkthrough: BACKWOODSMEN is the name for hereditary peers who seldom attend the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwoodsmen, in British politics, are members of the House of Lords who rarely come to sit.

clue.text: Go up to a price that's around 100

indicators.note: the price phrase goes around the hundred

parts.note: cost is a price
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Bidding for something that costs about a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly.

clue.text: To cut corners carelessly's right out

indicators.note: doing something carelessly mixes it up, so the letters are jumbled, the 's being is
out tells us the right letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A warning that sloppy shortcuts are not right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one R from CORNERS, leaving CONERS, which 'carelessly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor a book or film is to cut out material judged unacceptable.

clue.text: Plain house around centre of France

indicators.note: the house sits around the central letters

parts.note: a villa is a house

indicators.note: the centre of the country's name is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A modest house in the middle of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla, by extension from the default ice-cream flavour, means plain or ordinary.

clue.text: Land in a ring

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: Ground that sits in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a ring' reads like a description of the island, which is a ring of coral.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island, a piece of land encircling a lagoon.

clue.text: Tailback possibly recorded in TV presenter's equipment

indicators.note: a recording is something heard, so we want the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: a tailback is a long queue of cars, an auto queue

explanation.surface: A traffic jam captured on film for a TV report.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailback is British for a queue of traffic stretching back from a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the brand of teleprompter that scrolls the script for a newsreader.

clue.text: Combined honours between sporting and religious subjects? That's taking on something meaty!

indicators.note: the religious subject takes in the next word

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the sporting school subject
PPE (politics, philosophy and economics) is a combined honours degree at Oxford

indicators.note: the combined degree goes between the sporting and the religious subjects

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A degree course straddling sport and religion, presented as a hefty undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: PE, PPE and RI are standard British school and university subject abbreviations; 'taking' puts ON inside RI to make RONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried sausage, a classic meaty pizza topping.

clue.text: It's not your fans who clap you in these

definitions.text: It's not your fans who clap you in these

parts.words: It's not your fans who clap you in these
parts.note: clapping someone in chains is what captors do, the opposite of a fan's applause

explanation.surface: A wry remark that applause from fans is not the only kind of clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clap' here means to fasten quickly, as in 'clapped in chains', not to applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are shackles or fetters, which enemies or jailers clap on a prisoner.

clue.text: File capture failing to initialize

indicators.note: failing to initialize means the capture word loses its initial letter

parts.note: to grasp is to seize or capture

explanation.surface: A computer error: a screen capture file that will not start up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is computing; 'File' is the tool, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse file used to shape wood or metal.

clue.text: Get off with that girl from 'ackney around fringes of London rave

indicators.note: the get-off word goes around the outer letters

parts.note: to alight is to get off a bus or train

indicators.note: the fringes of the city's name are its first and last letters

parts.note: her said Cockney fashion, dropping the H as in 'ackney for Hackney, becomes 'er

explanation.surface: A Cockney chat-up line: pull that East End girl at a London party.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a district of East London; Cockneys traditionally drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-nighter is a party or dance that lasts the whole night, like a rave.
